nh_humphrey_s_ledge_2.blurb: Humphrey's Ledge is a granite cliff just west of North Conway, rising over the Saco River valley in the Mount Washington Valley. It has a quieter feel than the busier ledges nearby. Bouldering makes up the largest share, spread from V0 into the V8 range with plenty of easier problems, and traditional routes come next, with a smaller handful of sport lines. The roped climbing mostly runs from 5.6 to 5.12 and bunches up around 5.10. In winter the cliff also draws ice climbers to frozen seeps, with a modest number of WI3 and WI4 lines. The main sub-areas are Humphrey's Bouldering, The Geriatric Walls and Humphrey's Ledge Ice Climbs.

nc_pilot_mountain.blurb: Pilot Mountain is a 2,241-foot peak in Surry and Yadkin counties of the North Carolina Piedmont, near the town of Pinnacle. The climbing is on quartzite, with sport routes and top-ropes leading, a fair number of trad lines and a small bouldering offering. Grades run from 5.7 up to 5.12 and cluster at 5.10 and 5.11, with some easier lines and a few V0 to V4 boulder problems. Routes range from slabs to roofs, and most finish at bolted anchors. Cooler days and winter are popular, while summer can get hot. Amphitheater, Three Bears and Little Amphitheater are the biggest crags.

tn_lilly_boulders.blurb: Lilly Boulders is a forested boulder field in Tennessee’s Obed and Clear Creek country, an area of Cumberland Plateau sandstone that is climbed year-round. The boulders stand roughly 8 to over 20 feet tall, and the forest setting is shaded and peaceful. It is almost purely bouldering, with a very small trad component. Problems cover V0 up to the V8 range with a few harder ones above that, and the middle of the range is thick with V2 to V5 lines. Harder problems tend to be steep and overhanging. Transformer Boulder, Hemlock Boulder and Piano Boulder hold the most problems.

ut_schoolroom_the.blurb: The Schoolroom is a stacked quartzite cliff band on the east side of Ogden, Utah, stretching from the 22nd Street end to the 27th Street end, with Ogden Canyon on its north side and Taylor Canyon on its south. The rock is fractured quartzite, in two tiers and more in places. Sport climbing is the biggest share, with a strong trad contingent and a few mixed routes. Grades run mostly from 5.10 to 5.12, with a modest spread of easier climbs below. The main walls face west, so mornings are shaded and afternoons and evenings sunny, while the Alcove faces northwest and is shadier. Asbury Park, Tree Crack Area and Sunday Wall are among the bigger sub-areas.
